action: Place the transducer in the midline near the xiphoid process. Orient the indicator towards the head (sagittal plane).
interpretation: Identify the liver edge in the sagittal view.

action: With the liver edge clearly in view, slide the transducer over to the patient's right.
interpretation: Scan until the portal vein is clearly identified. Note the portal vein is surrounded by a bright layer of fascia.

action: Maintain position and observe the anatomy on the right side of the screen.
interpretation: Visualize the gallbladder connected to the portal vein.

action: Sweep through the gallbladder by bringing the top of the transducer all the way over to the left and all the way to the right.
interpretation: Inspect the gallbladder lumen to ensure there are no signs of stones or inflammation.

action: Rotate the transducer 90 degrees. Perform a second sweep through the entire body of the gallbladder.
interpretation: Obtain a second plane through the gallbladder. Pay special attention to the neck of the gallbladder during the sweep.

action: Return focus to the portal vein area and scan adjacent structures.
interpretation: Check for a 'second dilatation' near the portal vein to rule out choledocolithiasis.

action: Activate Color Mode (Color Doppler) over the area of interest.
interpretation: Use flow signals to distinguish anatomy: confirm the portal vein as a vascular structure and verify the gallbladder is clearly not vascular.
